text:
maya: Quick heads-up — after flipping on the FP8 kernel on L40s for model-x bring-up, our nightly eval shows a small but consistent quality regression. EM down ~2.6% and perplexity up ~0.7 across the QA benchmark. Repro steps and minimal logs below. :frowning:

maya: Repro (short):
```
env: GPU=L40S
runtime_flag: enable_fp8=true
quant_profile: fp8-e4m3
batch: 8
seq_len: 2048
tiling: auto
dynamic_scale: true
model: model-x:v2
```
maya: log snippet (inference trace):
```
[run] kernel=fp8_gemm_tiled version=2.1.4
[warn] layer_12: activation_scale clipped -> 1.23e-2
[info] fallback: layer_27 -> fp16 (nan detected)
[metric] EM=0.841 vs baseline 0.864
```

jordan: Did H100 runs see the same delta or only L40s?

maya: Only L40s so far. H100 canary with the same flag is within noise. L40s consistently worse across 3 seeds.

sam: Two immediate suspects: tiling/GEMM path differences between H100/L40s, or dynamic scaling behavior saturating on certain layers. Also check KV-cache interaction if you use streaming.

lisa: Related note — we saw a weird off-by-one KV-cache alignment when mixed-precision and continuous batching are combined. It caused subtle attention shifts but only in long-context (>=1024) runs. Could be the same family of bugs.

maya: We're not streaming; stateless evals. But we did bump seq_len from 1024->2048 for this model, so longer context may be exposing numerical edge cases.

jordan: Can you run two quick variants: (1) same config but `dynamic_scale=false` (fixed global scale), (2) `tiling=linear` (force non-autotiled GEMM). That will tell us if scaling vs tiling is dominant.

maya: Running now. ETA ~15m.

infra-bot: Canary run queued on l40s-pool-3 (job id: canary-1907654321-01).

maya: Results: variant (1) dynamic_scale=false -> EM == baseline (0.863). variant (2) tiling=linear -> EM 0.845 (still -2%).

sam: That strongly points to the dynamic scaling / FP8 scaling schedule triggering the regression. Tiling still matters but less.

lisa: Possible mechanism: the per-tensor scale estimator is under-estimating a tail activation for certain attention heads at long seq, resulting in clipped activations and tiny value truncation. That would explain why fixed scale avoids regression.

jordan: Any NaNs in the run with `dynamic_scale=true`? You had a fallback to fp16 in layer_27 above. Is that deterministic?

maya: Fallback happened in ~1/10 batches, consistent across seeds. No full-run crash, just local fallback and slight metric drift.

sam: Two experiments to add: dump per-layer activation scale stats (min/max/percentile) for the failing runs, and run with a slightly increased scale headroom (scale_clip_factor=1.5). Also try AWQ/GPTQ runs to see if non-FP8 quantized variants avoid the issue entirely.

maya: Will add dumps. Quick check: AWQ-int8 run on L40s produced EM 0.862 (close to baseline) but latency and memory differ.

lisa: That suggests FP8-specific scaling nuance. On H100 the kernel has a different per-op accumulation path which may mask the under-estimate. L40s fused kernel may use a tighter accumulator or different rounding that triggers the visible delta.

jordan: If we confirm it's scaling, short-term mitigations: keep `dynamic_scale=false` for L40s canary until we ship a kernel patch; or increase scale headroom. Long-term: update FP8 scale estimator to account for long-seq attention head tails and add regression tests in CI for seq_len >= 2048.

maya: Action items:
- maya: produce per-layer scale dumps + attach to this thread (today EOD).
- sam: add small repro that toggles scale_clip_factor and automates metric compute (tomorrow).
- lisa: file runtime kernel bug with vendor contacts, include tiling/accum path notes and attach perf traces (today).
- jordan: gate L40s rollout behind `dynamic_scale` flag until we have a patch (PR for feature flag rollback) (today).

maya: Quick logs I attached (pasted below) show layer_11/12/13 have 99.9th percentile spikes that dynamic_scale reduces aggressively — might be the immediate target.

lisa: Also add a CI canary that runs model-x on L40s at seq 2048 for both dynamic_scale true/false and fails if EM delta > 1%. That will catch regressions early.

sam: Good. If someone needs a short-term alternative for customers, AWQ-int8 is a decent stopgap for model-x on L40s until we ship the FP8 kernel fix.

maya: Thanks team — I'll post the dumps and a minimal repro notebook in ~2h. :thumbsup:

jordan: cheers. :eyes:

infra-bot: canary-1907654321-01 completed: 3/3 runs ok, flagged for triage.

maya: Closing loop for now, will update when dumps are uploaded.
